items.title: John Abercrombie interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, April 19, 2001
items.q: And before that I had worked with Billy Cobham, which was a great experience.

ctx.x: You seem to have had your tastes in a lot of different places. Has it always been of your own choosing?

No. I mean I think it gets mixed up. Sometimes it’s hard to know whether or not it’s your own choosing. Sometimes you find yourself in a situation that you think you wanted to get in and then once you’re in it you realize you shouldn’t be there. I’d say since I started playing this music, most of it’s been pretty much stuff I like to do. It hasn’t always been my own choosing. Sometimes somebody will hire me and I need the gig. Especially when I was younger and I would take any gig that was offered to me from the…

Michael and Randy. And then I got a phone call one morning from Jack DeJohnette and he just asked me if I wanted to come up and play at his house. And I said sure. So I went up and we played and we started a relationship, and that would sort of pull me back away from the pure fusion music and put me back closer to where I had started.
